homes.where: Hotel Corwin, room 9F (W 31st St, Broadway–6th Ave)
homes.why: The job comes with the room (N1). He lives where he works: eight by ten, one window on West Thirty-First Street: the Corwin's own broken neon (HOT  CO WIN) blinks red through it all night.

a hot plate and one pan

byAct.3: Hollis's radio on the sill (after M19); the ledger copy under the floorboard (if wire)
byAct.epilogue: packed (Testimony) / unchanged (Public) / a new suit on the door (New Pad) / bare (Ashes)

homes.where: Penn South co-op, a 7th-floor one-bedroom (W 27th St, 8th–9th Aves)
homes.why: Bought in 1965 as an ILGWU presser, when Penn South was union housing. She kept paying the maintenance when the work went south. Dignified, separate from Eighth Ave; nobody on the strip knows. Carmen Arce lives two buildings over, and they nod in the elevator.
portrait: the pressing iron she kept, on a shelf like a trophy
a sewing machine with a cover she made
a framed union card (1963)
her mother's photo from Wilmington
a green notebook she never writes in (decoy)
two good dresses and five practical ones
plants: a lot of plants

byAct.1: a beauty-shop magazine open on the table
byAct.2: prints drying on a string over the bath (the photo file)
byAct.3: the lease papers (if any) on the table; Tina's hairbrush in the bathroom (if she stays)
byAct.epilogue: a key to W 37th St on a nail (shop) or a joint ledger with Mi-sook (kye)

homes.note: Club cash still lives in the Arden boiler room (Marcus), not at home. That's her rule.

homes.where: A prewar doorman building, Madison Ave & E 37th St (11th floor)
homes.why: Grand, bought in 1968 at the top of his rise. The doorman (Cas Wojcik) is a barometer of his finances.
portrait: a grand piano nobody plays

amber worry beads on every table
a desk with a drawer of unpaid bills

a balcony with dead geraniums
